genesis/31/25.text: And Iacob had now pitched his tent in the mountaine: and when he with his brethren had ouertaben him, he pitched his tent in the ſame Mount Galaad. F

genesis/31/26.text: And he ſaid to Iacob: Vhy dideſt thou ſo, that vnwvitting to me thou vouldeſt carie away my daughters as captiues with the ſword?

genesis/31/27.text: I Vhy vouldeſt thou flee without my kno vledge, and not tel me, that I might haue brought thee on the way with ioy, and ſongues, and timbrels, and cithernes?

genesis/31/28.text: Thou haſt not ſuf¬ fred me to kiſſe my ſonnes and daughters: thou haſt donne fooliſſly: nov alſo in dede, τ

genesis/31/29.text: my hand is able to requite thee euil: but the God ofyour father ſaid vnto me yeſterday: Take hede thou ſpeake not any thing againſt Iacob roughly.

genesis/31/30.text: Suppoſe, thou diddeſt deſire to goe to thy freinds, and hadeſt a longingto thy fathers houſe: vhy dideſt thou ſteale

genesis/31/31.text: Iacob anſwered: In that I departed vnwitting to thee, I feared leſt thou wouldeſt take away thy daughters by force.

genesis/31/32.text: But wheras thou chargeſt me with theft: with whom ſoeuer thou ſhalt find thy goddes, let him be ſlaine before our brethen. ſearch, what ſoeuer of thy things thou ſhalt finde with me, and take away. Saying this, he knew not that Rachel had ſtollen the idols.

genesis/31/33.text: Laban therfore hauing gone into the tent of Iacob, and of Lia, and of both the hand. maides, found them not. And when he was entred into Rachels tent,

genesis/31/34.text: ſhe in haſt hid the idols vnder the camels litter, and ſatte therupon: and when he had ſought al the tent, and found nothing. ˣ

genesis/31/36.text: And Iacob this being:: angrie ſaid in chiding maner: For what fault of myne, expoſtula and for vhat offence of my part haſt thou ſo chaffed after me,

genesis/31/37.text: and ſearched al my hous hould ſtuffer Vhat haſt thou found of al the ſabſtance of thy houſer lay it here before my brethren, and thy brethren, and let them iudge bet wen me & thee. I

genesis/31/38.text: Haue I therfore bene with thee twentie yeares? thy ewes and goates were not barren, the wethers of thy flocke I did not eate: F

genesis/31/39.text: neyther that vhich the beaſt had caught did I shew to thec. I made good al the damage: whatſoeuer periſhed by theft, thou dideſt exact it of me:

genesis/31/40.text: day and night was I parched with heate, and with froſt, and ſleepe did flye from myne eyes.

genesis/31/41.text: And in this ſorte haue I ſerued thee in thy houſe twentie yeares, fourtene for thy daughters, and ſix for thy flockes: thou haſt changed alſo my wages tenne times.

genesis/31/42.text: Vnles the God ofmy father Abra¬ ham, and the feare of Iſaac had holpe me, peraduenture now thou haddeſt ſent me away naked: God bcheld my affliction and the laboure of my hands, and rebuked thee yeſterday.

genesis/31/43.text: Laban anſwered him: The daughters are mine and the children, and thy flockes, and al things that thou ſeeſt are mine: what can I do to my daughters, and ne¬ phews? F

genesis/31/44.text: Come therfore, let vs enter in league: that it may be for a teſtimonie bet ven me and thee.

genesis/31/45.text: Iacob ther¬ fore tooke a ſtone, and erected it for a title:

genesis/31/46.text: and he ſaid to his brethren: Bring hither ſtones. Vho gethering them together made a heape, and they did eate vpon it:

genesis/31/47.text: Laban called The vitneſſe heape: and Iacob called The hillock of teſtimonie, either of them according to the pro¬ prietie of his language.

genesis/31/48.text: And Laban ſaid: This heape ſhal be a witnes bet wen me and thee this day, and therfore the name therof was called Galaad, that is, The witnes heape. F

genesis/31/50.text: if thou ſhalt afflict my daughters, and ifthou bring in other wiues ouer them: none is witnes of our talke but God, who is preſent and behol¬ deth. F

genesis/31/51.text: And he ſaid againe to Iacob: Behold this heape, and the ſtone which I haue erected betven me and thec, I

genesis/31/52.text: ſhal be a witnes: this heape, I ſay, and the ſtone be they for a teſtimonie, if either I ſhal paſſe beyond it going to¬ wards thee, or thou ſhalt paſſe beyond it, thinking harme to me. F

genesis/31/53.text: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nachor iudge betwen vs, the God of their father. Iacob therfore ſware by the feare of his father Iſaac:

genesis/31/54.text: and after he had offred victimes in the mountaine, he called his brethren to eate bread. Vho when they had eaten, lodged there:

genesis/31/55.text: but Laban ariſing in the night, kiſſed his ſonnes, and daugh¬ ters, and bleſſed them: and returned vnto his place.

genesis/32/30.text: And lacob called the name ofthe place Phanuel, ſaying: I haue ſene God face to dit. Heb. face, aud my ſoule was made ſafe.

genesis/32/1.text: B alſo went on his iourney that he had begunne: L and the Angels of God met him.

genesis/32/2.text: F Vhom vhen he had ſeene, he ſaid: Theſe are the Campes of God, and he called the name of that place Mahanaim, that is, Campes.

genesis/32/3.text: And he ſent alſo meſſengers before him to Eſau his brother into the land of Seir, into the countrie of Edom:

genesis/32/4.text: and he com¬ manded them, ſaying: Thus ſpeake ye vnto my lord Eſau: This ſaith thy brother Iacob: I haue ſoiourned, and haue bene with Laban vntil this preſent day.

genesis/32/5.text: I haue oxen, and aſſes, and ſheepe, and men ſeruants, and wemen ſeruants: and now I ſend a leagacie to my lord, that I may finde grace in thy ſight.

genesis/32/6.text: And the meſſengers returned to Iacob, ſaying: Ve came to Eſau thy brother, and behold he cometh vith ſpede to mete thee with foure hundred men.

genesis/32/7.text: Iacob feared exceedingly: & being ſore affraid diuided the people that was with him, the flockes alſo and the ſhepe and the oxen, and the camels, into two troupes,

genesis/32/8.text: ſaying: If Eſau come to one troupe, and ſtrike it, the other troupe that remaineth, mhal be ſaued.

genesis/32/9.text: And Iacob ſaid: O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Iſaac: O Lord that dideſt ſay to me: Returne into thy land, and into the place of thy natiuitie, and I wil doc thee good.

genesis/32/10.text: I am inferiourto al thy mercies, and thy truth that thou haſt fulfilled to thy ſeruant. Vith my ſtaffe I paſſed ouer this Iordain: and now with two troupes I doe returne.

genesis/32/11.text: Deliuer me from the hand of my brother Eſau, becauſe I am ſore affraid ofhim: leſt perhaps he come, and ſtrike the mother with the chil¬ dren. F

genesis/32/12.text: and dilate my ſeed as the ſand ofthe ſea, which for multitude can not be numbred. F

genesis/32/13.text: And vhen he had ſlept there that night, he ſeparated of thoſe things vhich he had, giftes to his brother Eſau, τͣ

genesis/32/14.text: ſhe goates two hundred, he goates twentie, ewes two hundred, and rammes twontie, ˣ thirtie

genesis/32/15.text: milch camels with their coltes, fourtie kine, and twentie bulles, twentie ſhe aſſes, and their foles ten.

genesis/32/16.text: And he ſent by the handes of his ſeruants, euerie flocke by it ſelfe, and he ſaid to his ſeruants: Goe before me, and let there be a ſpace betwen flocke and flocke.

genesis/32/17.text: And he commanded the former, ſaying: If thou mete my brother Eſau, and he aske thee, vhoſe art thour or whither goeſt thour or vhoſe are theſe that thou doeſt folower

genesis/32/18.text: thou ſhalt anſwere: Iacobes thy ſeruant, he hath ſent them for gifts to my lord Eſau: himſelfe alſo cometh after vs.

genesis/32/19.text: In like maner he gaue commandements to the ſecond, and the third, and to al that folowed the flocks, ſaying: Vith the ſelfe ſamc vords ſpeake yc to Eſau, when you ſhal finde him.

genesis/32/20.text: And ye ſhal adde: Iacob alſo thy ſeruant himſelfe foloweth on after vsꝫ for he ſaid: I wil pacifie him with the gifts that goe before, and afterward I wil ſec him, perhaps he wil be gracious vnto me.

genesis/32/21.text: The giftes therfore vent before him, but himſelfe lodged that night in the campe.

genesis/32/22.text: And vhen he was riſen early he tooke his tvo wiues, and his hand¬ maides as manie, with his eleuen ſonnes, and paſſed ouer the ford Iaboc.

genesis/32/23.text: And vhen he had ſet ouer al things that appertained to him,

genesis/32/24.text: he taried alone: and behold/ a man wraſteled with him. til morning.

genesis/32/25.text: F Vho vlien he ſaw that he could not ouercome him, he touched the ſinowe of his thighe, and forthwith it ſhranke.

genesis/32/26.text: And he ſaid to him: Let me goe for it is breake of day. He anſwered: I wil not let thec goe, vnleſſe thou bleſſe me.

genesis/32/27.text: He therfore ſaid: Vhat is thy namer He anſwered: Iacob.

genesis/32/28.text: But he, no, thy name, quoth he,:: ſhal not be called Iacob, but Iſrael: for if thou ging of his haſt bene ſtrong againſt God, how much more shalt thou pre. hame herc uaile againſt men?

genesis/32/29.text: Iacob asked him: Tel me by what name promiſed, is art thou called? He anſvered: Vhy doeſt thou aske my namer performed and bleſſed him in the ſamc place.

genesis/32/31.text: And immediatly the ſunne roſe to him, after that he vas paſt Phanuel; but he

genesis/32/32.text: For vhich cauſe the children of Iſrael eate not the ſinowe, that ſhrunke in Iacobes thighe, vnto his preſent day: becauſe he touched the ſinowe of his thighe, and it ſhrunke.

genesis/33/1.text: and Iacob lifting vp his eyes, ſaw Eſau coming, and X with him foure hundred men: and he diuided the chil¬ dren of Lia and of Rachel, and of the two handmaides: Fͣ

genesis/33/2.text: and he put both the handmaids & their children foremoſt: and Lia, and her children in the ſecond place: and Rachel, and Ioſeph laſt.

genesis/33/3.text: And himſelfe going foreward adored pro¬ ſtrate to the grovnd ſeuen times, vntil his brother came nere. F

genesis/33/4.text: Eſau therfore running to mete his brother, em¬ braced him: and claſping him faſt about the necke, and kiſſing him wept.

genesis/33/5.text: And caſting vp his eyes, he ſaw the wemen and their litle ones, and ſaid: Vhat meane theſe: And do they perteyne to thee? He anſwered: They are the litle ones which God hath geuen to me thy ſeruant.

genesis/33/6.text: And the handmaides and their children coming nere, bowed themſelues.

genesis/33/7.text: Lia alſo with her children came nere: and when they had adored in like maner, laſt Ioſeph and Rachel adored.

genesis/33/8.text: And Eſau ſaid: Vhat are the troupes that I did mete? He anſwered: That I might find grace before my lord.

genesis/33/9.text: But he ſaid: I haue plentie, my brother, be thy things to thy ſelfe. F

genesis/33/10.text: And Iacob ſaid: Do not ſo I beſech thee, but if I haue found grace in thin cyes, take a litle preſent at my hands: for ſo haue I ſeene thy face, as if I ſhould haue ſeene II:: the countenance of God: be gracious to me,

genesis/33/11.text: and take:: Iacob ſeins the bleſſing, vhich I haue brought thee, and which God Gods hand in hath geuen me, who geueth al thinges. Scarſe at his brothers this change of great inſtance, taking it,

genesis/33/12.text: he ſaid: Let vs march on toge. ther, and I wil accompanie thee in thy iourney.

genesis/33/13.text: flaterie. but cob ſaid: My lord thou knoweſt that I haue with me litle ſincerly ac¬ ones, and ſheepe, and kinc with young: which if I cauſe knowledged to ouerlaboure themſelues in going, in one day al the flockes wil die.

genesis/33/14.text: It may pleaſe my lord to goe before his ſeruant̉: renance to¬ and I wil folov ſoftly after him, as I ſhal ſee my litle ones vards him.

genesis/33/15.text: Eſau anſwe. red: I beſech thee, that ofmy people at the leaſtwiſe, vhich is with me, there may remaine ſome to accompanie thee in the way. It is not needful, ſaid he, this only I haue nede of, that I may finde grace (my lord) in thy ſight.

genesis/33/16.text: Eſau ther. fore returned that day the ſame way, that he came into Seir.

genesis/33/17.text: And Iacob cometh into Socoth: vhere hauing built a houſe, and pitched his tents, he called the name of that place Socoth, that is. Tabernacles.

genesis/33/18.text: And he paſſed into Salem a citie ofthe Sichimites, which is in the land of Cha¬ naan, after he returned from Meſopotamia of Siria: and he dwelt beſide the towne.

genesis/33/19.text: And he bought that part of the field, vherin he had pitched his tents, of the children of Hemor, the father fo. Sichem for an hundred lambes.

genesis/33/20.text: And erecting an altar there, on it he called vpon the moſt mightie God of Iſrael.

genesis/34/1.text: ND Dina the daughter of Lia vent forth:: to ſce the L wemen of that countrie.

genesis/34/2.text: Vhom when Sichem had ſeene the ſonne of Hemor the Heuite, the prince of that land, he was in loue with her: and he tooke her away, and lay with her, by force rauiſhing the virgin.

genesis/34/3.text: And his ſoule was faſt kint vnto her, and vheras ſne vas ſad, he com¬ forted her with ſweete wordes. I

genesis/34/4.text: And going to Hemor his father, he laid: Take me this venchoto be my wife.

genesis/34/5.text: Vhich when Iacob had heard, his ſonnes beingabſent, and occupied in feeding ofthe cattle, he held his peace til they returned.

genesis/34/6.text: And vhen Hemor Sichems father was come forth to ſpeake vnto Iacob,

genesis/34/7.text: his ſonnes came out of the field: and lcaring vhat had paſſed, they vere paſſing virath, becauſe he had done a foule thingin Iſrael, and committed an vnla wful fact, in raui ſhing Iacobs daugh¬ ter F

genesis/34/8.text: Hemor therfore ſpake to them: The ſoule of my ſonne Sichem is faſtned to your daughter: Geue her vnto him to

genesis/34/9.text: and let vs contract mariages onc vith an other: geue vs your daughters, and take you our daughters.

genesis/34/10.text: And d vel vith vs: the land is at your commandement, tille, oc¬ cupie, and poſſeſſe it.

genesis/34/11.text: Yea and Sichem alſo ſaid to her father and to her brethren: Let me finde grace in your ſight: and what ſoeuer you ſhal appointe I wil geue:

genesis/34/12.text: raiſe the do vrie, and require giftes, and I ſhal gladly geue, vhat you ſhal demande: only geue me this wenchito wiſe. F

genesis/34/13.text: Iacobs ſonnes anſwered Sichem & his father:: in guile, being wrath:: Thcy offen¬ for the deflouring of their ſiſter:

genesis/34/14.text: Ve can not doc that ded by falſly which you demande, nor geue our ſiſter to an vncircumciſed perſon: vhich vith vs is an vnla vful & abhominable thing.

genesis/34/15.text: But in this order ve may be confederate, if you wil be uenge, & ther¬ like to vs, and al the man ſex among you be circumciſed:

genesis/34/16.text: then wil we geue and take mutually your daughters, and ours: and we wil dwel vith you, and wil be one people:

genesis/34/17.text: but ifyou vil not be circumciſed, we wil take our daugh. Otherviſc ter, and depart.

genesis/34/18.text: The offer pleaſed Hemor, and Sichem their reale vas his ſonne:

genesis/34/19.text: neither did the young man make delay, but forthwith fulfilled that which was demanded: for he loued the wench exceedingly, and he vas the greateſt man in al his fathers houſe.

genesis/34/20.text: And going into tlie gate of the citie, they ſpake to the people:

genesis/34/21.text: Theſe men are men of peace, and are willing to dwel with vs: let them occupie in the land, and til it, which being large. and wide doth lacke men to tille it: their daugliters ve ſhal take to wife. and ours we wil geue to them.

genesis/34/22.text: One thing there is for the which ſo great a goodis differred: If we circumciſe our men ſexe, folowing the rite of the nation.

genesis/34/23.text: And their ſubſtance, and cattle, and al things that they poſſeſſe, ſhal be ours: only in this let vs condeſcend, and dwelling togeather, ve ſhal make one people.

genesis/34/24.text: And they al aſſented, and circumciſed al the man ſex.

genesis/34/25.text: And behold the third day, vben the griefe of the voundes is moſt paineful: Iacobs two ſonnes, Simeon and Leui the brothers of Dina taking their ſwordes, entred into the citie boldly: and killing al the man ſex,

genesis/34/26.text: murdred v ithal Hemor and Sichem, taking away Dina their ſiſter out of Sichems houſe.

genesis/34/27.text: Vhen they were gone forth, the other ſonnes of Iacob ranne in vpon them that vere ſlaine: and ſpoiled the citie in reuenge of the rape.

genesis/34/28.text: And vaſting al things that vere in their houſes, and fildes, their ſhecpe and

genesis/35/3.text: Ariſe, and let vs goe vp into Bethel, that we may make there an altar vnto God: who heard me in the day of my tribulation, and ac¬ compained me in my iourney.

genesis/35/4.text: They gaue to him therfore al the ſtrange goddes that they had, and the earelets which were in their eares: but he buried them vnder ther terebinth. that is behind the citie of Sichem.

genesis/35/5.text: And vhen they vere departed,:: the terror of God inuaded al the cities rounde about, and they durſt not purſew them goingaway. F

genesis/35/6.text: And Iacob came to Luza, whichis in the land of Chanaan, ſur¬ mightie; named Bethel: he and al the people that was with him.

genesis/35/7.text: And he builded there an altar, and called the name of that place, The houſe of God: for there God appeared to him vhen he fled from his brother.

genesis/35/9.text: to Iacob after he returned from Meſopotamia of Siria, and he bleſſed him, τ

genesis/35/10.text: ſaying: Thou:: ſhalt not be called any more:: The name of Iacob, but Iſrael ſhal be thy name. And he called him ſupplanter not Iſrael,

genesis/35/11.text: and ſaid to him: I am God almightie, encreaſe thou and multiplic: Of thec ſhal be nations and peoples of na¬ lurc he is alſo tions, kinges ſhal come forth of thy loynes.

genesis/35/15.text: and calling the name of that place, Bethel.

genesis/35/18.text: And her ſoule departing for paīne, and death nov at hand, she called the name of her ſonne Benoni, that is the ſonne ofmy paine: but his father called him Beniamin. that is the ſonne ofthe right hand.

genesis/35/19.text: Rachel therfore died, and vas buried in the hye way that leadeth to Ephrata, this ſame is Bethleem.

genesis/35/20.text: And Iacob erected a title ouerher ſe¬ pulchre: This is the litle of Rachels monument, vntil this preſent day.

genesis/35/21.text: Departing thence, he pitched his tent beyond the Flocke tower.

genesis/35/22.text: And vhen he d velt in that countrie: Ruben vent, and:: ſlept vith Bala his fathers con¬:: For this fact cubine: which thinghe was not ignorant of. And the ſonnes of Iacob vere twelue.

genesis/35/23.text: The ſonnes of Lia: Ruben the the chiefedig¬ firſt begotten, and Simeon, and Leui, and Iudas, and Iſſachar, nitie among and Zabulon.

genesis/34/29.text: their little ones alſo, and their viues they led away captiue.

genesis/34/30.text: Vhich things vhen they had boldly atcheiued, Iacob ſaid to Simeon and Leui: You haue trubled me, and made me odious to the Chananites, and Pherezites the inhabiters of this land. we are few: they being gethered together wil ſtrike meꝫ and I, and my houſe ſhal be deſtroyed.

genesis/34/31.text: They anſwered: Vhat ſhould they abuſe our ſiſter as a ſtrumpet?

genesis/35/1.text: in the time God ſpake to Iacob: Ariſe, and goe x L vp to Bethel, and dwel there, and make an altar to God that appeared to thee when thou diddeſt flie from Eſau thy brother. F

genesis/35/2.text: And Iacob hauing called together al his houſc, ſaid: Caſt away the ſtrange goddes that are among you, and be clenſed and change your garments.

genesis/35/8.text: The ſame time died in Debora the nurſe of Rebecca, and vas buried at the foote of Bethel vnder an obe: and the name of that place was called, The okc of veeping.

genesis/35/12.text: And the land called Iſrael. vhich I gaue to Abraham and Iſaac, I vil geue to thee, and Sec the Anno¬ to thy ſeede after thee.

genesis/35/14.text: But he erected a title ofſtone, in the place vhere God had ſpoken vnto him: offering vpon it liquide offeringes, and powring oile on it:

genesis/35/16.text: And being gone forth from thence, he came in the ſpring time to the land vhich leadeth to Ephrata: vherin when Rachel was in trauaile.

genesis/35/17.text: becauſe of diffi¬ cultie in her trauaile, ſhe beganne to be in danger, and the midwife ſaid vnto her: Feare not, for thou shalt haue alſo this a ſonne.

genesis/35/24.text: The ſonnes of Rachel: Ioſeph and Ben¬

genesis/35/25.text: The ſonnes of Bala Rachels handmaid: Dan and Nepthali.

genesis/35/26.text: The ſonnes of Zelpha Lias handmaid: Gad and Aſer: theſe are the ſonnes of Iacob, that vere borne to him in Meſopotamia of Siria.

genesis/35/27.text: He came alſo to Iſaac his father in Mambre, the citie of Arbee, this is Hebron: wherin Abraham and Iſaac ſoiourned.

genesis/35/28.text: And the dayes of Iſaac vere complete an hundred eyghtie yeares. f

genesis/35/29.text: And ſpent Vith age he died, and was put to his people, being old and ful ofdayes: and Eſau and Iacob his ſonnes buryed him.

genesis/36/1.text: and theſe are the generations of Eſau, the ſame is I X Edom. I

genesis/36/2.text: Eſau tooke wiues of the daughters of Cha. naan: Ada the daughter of Elon the Hetheite, and Ooli¬ bama the daughter of Ana daughter of Sebeon the Heueite:

genesis/36/3.text: Baſemath alſo the daughter of Iſmael ſiſter of Nabaioth.
